# Lonely Grief-Bound

**Family:** Grief-Bound
**Knowledge status:** Restricted Deep Record
**Publication classification:** Deep-license reference
**Dungeon range:** T4-T5, Floors 31-50
**Primary source:** Hospice accounts, survivor interviews, and censored temple memoranda
**Reliability:** Moderate to high
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

This Grief-Bound is absence that divides a group into private rooms of memory. It hunts emotional repetition rather than flesh alone, and it grows more coherent whenever the Expedition reenacts the behavior that created it.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

A memory repeated by people who were not present; food spoiling only after it is counted; camp chairs facing an empty place; wounds aching in response to an unrelated argument. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Religion** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 14 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 18 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 22 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Restricted Deep Record  
**Primary source:** Hospice accounts, survivor interviews, and censored temple memoranda  
**Reliability:** Moderate to high  
**Last confirmed:** Confirmed within the last two Openings  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 31-40  
**Rumored range:** Floors 41-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Survivors report memories that do not belong to any known casualty. The Haven hospice forbids recording these accounts in the witness’s own handwriting. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Large Undead, Neutral**  
**Challenge** 15 (13000 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T4-T5 · **Floors** 31-50
**Armor** 18 · **Hit Points** 494 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 18 (+4) | 15 (+2) | 19 (+4) | 10 (+0) | 15 (+2) | 17 (+3) |

**Resistances** necrotic  
**Immunities** poison  
**Condition Immunities** poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** breaking the emotional loop  
**Save DC** 18  

### Traits

**Emotional Feeding.** When a nearby creature performs the behavior that defines this Grief-Bound, it gains temporary hit points equal to its tier.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Isolating Touch.** *Attack:* +9 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d10+10 psychic damage (average 26).

**Surge Bolt.** *Attack:* +9 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d10+9 lightning damage (average 26).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Isolating Touch** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Surge Bolt** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It attacks the character whose behavior most closely matches its defining loss.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic, lightning damage.
- Agree on verbal and physical contact signals before entry.

**Combat Priority**

Identify the repeated emotion and stop feeding it before striking the exposed core.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **breaking the emotional loop**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line; resources fall below half before the arena mechanic is solved. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Their territory accumulates symbolic objects. Destroying every object can strengthen the entity by confirming its loss; identifying the central memory is safer.

Grief-Bound are emotional deaths that found enough matter or Resonance to keep moving. They are not ordinary ghosts. Each is a self-reinforcing need that hunts situations capable of repeating the moment that made it.

Some can be quieted, redirected, or released if the original loss is understood. False promises often produce a stronger return.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Arcana · **Harvest DC:** 15 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Elemental Core (Tier 1) | 1 | 100%, 25 gp base |
| Pure Element (Tier 2) | 2 | 94%, 50 gp base |
| Primal Essence (Tier 3) | 3 | 75%, 100 gp base |
| Elemental Shard (Tier 4) | 4 | 56%, 200 gp base |
| Elemental Shard (Tier 5) | 5 | 38%, 400 gp base |

Residual emotion can be captured as grief-salt, memory ash, or a bound echo. Such material is useful in Scribing, Enchanting, and necromantic research but carries contamination risk.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the originating loss, feeding behavior, and release condition. The same combat block can represent different tragedies only when the emotional counter also changes.

# Lumen Drifter

**Family:** Void
**Knowledge status:** Restricted Deep Record
**Publication classification:** Deep-license reference
**Dungeon range:** T4-T5, Floors 31-50
**Primary source:** Navigator logs, damaged observatory plates, and recovered expedition journals
**Reliability:** Moderate to high
**Encounter role:** Striker

## What It Is

Lumen Drifter treats distance and possession as negotiable states. It can make separation feel like movement and can turn an apparently empty container, corridor, or memory into an attack vector.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Shadows pointing toward different lights; containers heavier when empty; spoken names missing from echoes; objects arriving before the hand releases them. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Restricted Deep Record  
**Primary source:** Navigator logs, damaged observatory plates, and recovered expedition journals  
**Reliability:** Moderate to high  
**Last confirmed:** Confirmed within the last two Openings  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 31-40  
**Rumored range:** Floors 41-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Several routes appear to curve around an absent mass. Surveyors agree on the distortion but not on what could produce it. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Large Elemental, Neutral**  
**Challenge** 6 (2300 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T4-T5 · **Floors** 31-50
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 224 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 17 (+3) | 14 (+2) | 17 (+3) | 8 (-1) | 11 (+0) | 9 (-1) |

**Resistances** poison  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** stable anchors and force wards  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Anchored Absence.** Teleportation and forced movement used against it are unreliable until an anchor object in the encounter is activated or destroyed.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Void Rend.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+6 psychic damage (average 15).

**Psychic Pulse.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+5 psychic damage (average 14).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Void Rend** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Psychic Pulse** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It isolates one target and makes the rest of the party spend actions proving where that target is.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic damage.
- Tether the team to stable anchor points.

**Combat Priority**

Protect memory and positioning; force the creature to act inside anchored space.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **stable anchors and force wards**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Void sites contain anchor stones, folded corridors, suspended debris, and pockets where sound or light fails. Destroying an anchor can open a worse route.

Void entities manipulate distance, ownership, memory, and absence. Some are predators; others are collectors or refugees whose presence makes ordinary navigation unreliable.

Brokers value unique experiences and impossible cargo. Archivists respect accurate records. Drifters may respond to restored light paths.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Arcana · **Harvest DC:** 14 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Giant Bone (Tier 1) | 1 | 72%, 16 gp base |
| Massive Tooth (Tier 2) | 2 | 60%, 32 gp base |
| pulsing brain stem | 3 | 48%, 64 gp base |

**Known recipe links:** Ascendant Mindclear Tincture, Minor Mindward Imbuement: Wand, Relic Gale Contact, Ascendant Ember Injury.

Void-warped eyes, alien chitin, memory crystals, lumen residue, and folded membranes require warded containers and careful provenance.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the anchor, object of trade, and kind of absence being manipulated. Avoid repeating ordinary teleportation as the only trick.

# Lumen of the Shattered Thread — The Sixth Gate Disaster Record

**Family:** Gate Guardian  
**Knowledge status:** Historical Failure Record  
**Publication classification:** Public history with restricted tactical annex  
**Dungeon range:** T6, Floors 51-60  
**Primary source:** The Sixth Gate Disaster Archive  
**Reliability:** High that the encounter occurred; fragmentary on exact mechanics  
**Encounter role:** Unconquered Gate Guardian

## What the World Knows

The most famous recognized expedition in Aethel reached the Sixth Gate and confronted the entity its surviving records call **Lumen of the Shattered Thread**. The expedition did not pass. Its failure defines the accepted limit of mortal descent.

The public record confirms a Gate arena, severe radiant and displacing effects, the collapse of formation discipline, and a final retreat that returned only fragments of the original company. No complete victory condition survives. Different copies disagree about how many people reached the arena and whether the retreat was voluntary.

## Signs Recorded Before Contact

- Reflections continued moving after the expedition stopped.
- Tether lines returned tied in unfamiliar knots.
- Written orders lost conjunctions, changing cooperation into mutually exclusive commands.
- Light sources illuminated different routes for different observers.
- The final camp contained preparation caches rather than sleeping spaces.

## What Failed

| Attempt | Recorded Result |
|---|---|
| Concentrated frontal assault | The formation was divided and support could no longer verify targets. |
| Independent flanking teams | Teams returned with incompatible memories of the arena. |
| Repeated radiant protection | Reduced casualties but did not solve the Gate principle. |
| Forced retreat after the first phase | Preserved a fraction of the expedition but abandoned wounded and records. |
| Destroying visible anchors | Some anchors reappeared in different positions. |

## What May Help

These are professional hypotheses, not proven solutions:

- Redundant command methods that do not depend on one voice, map, reflection, or light source.
- Physical tethers marked by touch as well as sight.
- Prearranged authority for retreat so contradictory orders cannot split the company.
- A Research team dedicated to the Gate principle rather than damage output.
- A willingness to abandon the attempt before the support line loses shared reality.

## How to Defeat It

**No verified method exists.** This manual does not provide a complete stat block, exact save DCs, or a guaranteed counter because the world of Aethel does not possess them. Reaching the Sixth Gate is a historical achievement. Passing it has no confirmed public record.

## Director Boundary

No public combat block exists. The Director should build on this incomplete record and allow characters to improve it only through play, recovered evidence, and direct observation.

---
*Compiled from the recognized Sixth Gate expedition’s surviving archive. Contradictory testimony has been preserved rather than silently reconciled.*

# Order-Drone Pair

**Family:** Order Drone
**Knowledge status:** Restricted Deep Record
**Publication classification:** Deep-license reference
**Dungeon range:** T4-T5, Floors 31-50
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies
**Reliability:** Moderate to high
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

Order-Drone Pair is a distributed containment intelligence. Its bodies are dangerous individually, but the real weapon is the geometry they maintain between one another and the terrain.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Evenly spaced scoring on stone; dust cleared in repeated arcs; metallic clicks answering one another around corners; corpses moved out of pathways rather than looted. Loose metal turns to face the same direction.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Engineering or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 13 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 17 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 21 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Restricted Deep Record  
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies  
**Reliability:** Moderate to high  
**Last confirmed:** Confirmed within the last two Openings  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 31-40  
**Rumored range:** Floors 41-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Formations occasionally protect empty chambers while ignoring valuable machinery. Their geometry implies an objective the observers cannot see. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Huge Construct, Neutral Good**  
**Challenge** 12 (8400 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T4-T5 · **Floors** 31-50
**Armor** 17 · **Hit Points** 404 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 22 (+6) | 13 (+1) | 20 (+5) | 9 (-1) | 10 (+0) | 7 (-2) |

**Resistances** poison, psychic  
**Immunities** disease  
**Condition Immunities** charmed, exhaustion, poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** forced movement that breaks formation  
**Save DC** 17  

### Traits

**Formation Intelligence.** While within 20 feet of another body in its unit, it gains +1 Armor and cannot be surprised.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Iron Slam.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d8+9 bludgeoning damage (average 22).

**Grinding Gear.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d8+8 bludgeoning damage (average 22).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Iron Slam** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Grinding Gear** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It uses every action to preserve formation and converts broken lines into immediate repositioning.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning damage.
- Bring forced movement and terrain creation.

**Combat Priority**

Split the formation and destroy the coordinating body.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **forced movement that breaks formation**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line; resources fall below half before the arena mechanic is solved. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Drone zones favor grids, choke points, rotating doors, magnetic floors, and lines that improve formation attacks. Their positions are part of the stat block.

Order-Drones are collective constructs designed to solve movement, trespass, and containment problems through formation. A “pair,” “tetrad,” or “quintet” is one tactical intelligence distributed across several bodies.

Correct credentials, maintenance codes, or a higher-priority emergency may redirect them. Emotional appeals do nothing unless the automaton was built to interpret them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Engineering · **Harvest DC:** 15 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Fey Dust (Tier 1) | 1 | 99%, 22 gp base |
| fused cog | 2 | 83%, 44 gp base |
| power node | 3 | 66%, 88 gp base |
| mana pipe | 4 | 50%, 176 gp base |

**Known recipe links:** Greater Arcane Salvaging Kit, Exalted Arcane Automaton.

Servo nodes, memory plates, conductive wire, command lenses, and intact housings are prime Tinkering and Enchanting components.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change formation size, command priority, and terrain. Each added body should expand tactical geometry rather than simply add attacks.

# Order-Drone Quintet

**Family:** Order Drone
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

Order-Drone Quintet is a distributed containment intelligence. Its bodies are dangerous individually, but the real weapon is the geometry they maintain between one another and the terrain.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Evenly spaced scoring on stone; dust cleared in repeated arcs; metallic clicks answering one another around corners; corpses moved out of pathways rather than looted. Loose metal turns to face the same direction.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Engineering or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 13 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 17 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 21 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Formations occasionally protect empty chambers while ignoring valuable machinery. Their geometry implies an objective the observers cannot see. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Huge Construct, True Neutral**  
**Challenge** 10 (5900 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 17 · **Hit Points** 344 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 21 (+5) | 13 (+1) | 19 (+4) | 8 (-1) | 10 (+0) | 7 (-2) |

**Resistances** poison, psychic  
**Immunities** disease  
**Condition Immunities** charmed, exhaustion, poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** forced movement that breaks formation  
**Save DC** 16  

### Traits

**Formation Intelligence.** While within 20 feet of another body in its unit, it gains +1 Armor and cannot be surprised.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Stone Fist.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+9 bludgeoning damage (average 20).

**Grinding Gear.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+8 bludgeoning damage (average 19).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Stone Fist** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Grinding Gear** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It uses every action to preserve formation and converts broken lines into immediate repositioning.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning damage.
- Bring forced movement and terrain creation.

**Combat Priority**

Split the formation and destroy the coordinating body.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **forced movement that breaks formation**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Drone zones favor grids, choke points, rotating doors, magnetic floors, and lines that improve formation attacks. Their positions are part of the stat block.

Order-Drones are collective constructs designed to solve movement, trespass, and containment problems through formation. A “pair,” “tetrad,” or “quintet” is one tactical intelligence distributed across several bodies.

Correct credentials, maintenance codes, or a higher-priority emergency may redirect them. Emotional appeals do nothing unless the automaton was built to interpret them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Engineering · **Harvest DC:** 14 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| servo node | 2 | Director-set |
| memory plate | 2 | Director-set |
| conductive wire | 2 | Director-set |

Servo nodes, memory plates, conductive wire, command lenses, and intact housings are prime Tinkering and Enchanting components.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change formation size, command priority, and terrain. Each added body should expand tactical geometry rather than simply add attacks.

# Order-Drone Tetrad

**Family:** Order Drone
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T1, Floors 1-10
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

Order-Drone Tetrad is a distributed containment intelligence. Its bodies are dangerous individually, but the real weapon is the geometry they maintain between one another and the terrain.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Evenly spaced scoring on stone; dust cleared in repeated arcs; metallic clicks answering one another around corners; corpses moved out of pathways rather than looted. Loose metal turns to face the same direction.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Engineering or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 11 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 15 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 19 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 1-10  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Small Construct, Chaotic Good**  
**Challenge** 1/4 (50 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T1 · **Floors** 1-10
**Armor** 11 · **Hit Points** 18 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 9 (-1) | 16 (+3) | 16 (+3) | 8 (-1) | 10 (+0) | 6 (-2) |

**Resistances** poison, psychic  
**Immunities** disease  
**Condition Immunities** charmed, exhaustion, poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** forced movement that breaks formation  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Formation Intelligence.** While within 20 feet of another body in its unit, it gains +1 Armor and cannot be surprised.

### Actions

**Iron Slam.** *Attack:* +3 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d6+1 bludgeoning damage (average 4).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Iron Slam** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses every action to preserve formation and converts broken lines into immediate repositioning.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning damage.
- Bring forced movement and terrain creation.

**Combat Priority**

Split the formation and destroy the coordinating body.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **forced movement that breaks formation**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Drone zones favor grids, choke points, rotating doors, magnetic floors, and lines that improve formation attacks. Their positions are part of the stat block.

Order-Drones are collective constructs designed to solve movement, trespass, and containment problems through formation. A “pair,” “tetrad,” or “quintet” is one tactical intelligence distributed across several bodies.

Correct credentials, maintenance codes, or a higher-priority emergency may redirect them. Emotional appeals do nothing unless the automaton was built to interpret them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Engineering · **Harvest DC:** 11 · **Base time:** 20 minutes  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Animated Core (Tier 1) | 1 | 46%, 10 gp base |

Servo nodes, memory plates, conductive wire, command lenses, and intact housings are prime Tinkering and Enchanting components.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change formation size, command priority, and terrain. Each added body should expand tactical geometry rather than simply add attacks.

# Pact Automaton Sentinel

**Family:** Order Drone
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T1, Floors 1-3
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Controller

## What It Is

Pact Automaton Sentinel is a distributed containment intelligence. Its bodies are dangerous individually, but the real weapon is the geometry they maintain between one another and the terrain.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Evenly spaced scoring on stone; dust cleared in repeated arcs; metallic clicks answering one another around corners; corpses moved out of pathways rather than looted. Loose metal turns to face the same direction.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Engineering or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 11 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 15 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 19 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 1-3  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Large Construct, Lawful Neutral**  
**Challenge** 6 (2300 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T1 · **Floors** 1-3
**Armor** 18 · **Hit Points** 145 · **Speed** 30 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 17 (+3) | 14 (+2) | 18 (+4) | 8 (-1) | 10 (+0) | 6 (-2) |

**Resistances** poison, psychic  
**Immunities** disease  
**Condition Immunities** charmed, exhaustion, poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** forced movement that breaks formation  
**Save DC** 15  

### Traits

**Formation Intelligence.** While within 20 feet of another body in its unit, it gains +1 Armor and cannot be surprised.

**Escalation Pulse.** **Containment Pulse** recharges on 5-6; visible signs appear one round before the first use.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 2 attacks using the actions below.

**Sentinel Halberd.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+5 slashing damage (average 16).

**Pressure Wave.** One target must succeed on a DC 15 save or take 3d8 force damage and suffer the action’s described control effect.

**Containment Pulse (Recharge 5-6).** Creatures in the affected area make a DC 15 Strength save, taking 5d6 force damage (average 18) on a failure and half on a success. The Director should describe the charge-up before resolving it.

## How It Fights

It opens with **Sentinel Halberd** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Pressure Wave** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. When **Containment Pulse** recharges, it delays only if it can catch a more important cluster or interrupt a decisive ritual. It uses every action to preserve formation and converts broken lines into immediate repositioning.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing, force damage.
- Spread before **Containment Pulse** becomes available.
- Bring forced movement and terrain creation.

**Combat Priority**

Split the formation and destroy the coordinating body.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **forced movement that breaks formation**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when Containment Pulse catches three or more Expedition members. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Drone zones favor grids, choke points, rotating doors, magnetic floors, and lines that improve formation attacks. Their positions are part of the stat block.

Order-Drones are collective constructs designed to solve movement, trespass, and containment problems through formation. A “pair,” “tetrad,” or “quintet” is one tactical intelligence distributed across several bodies.

Correct credentials, maintenance codes, or a higher-priority emergency may redirect them. Emotional appeals do nothing unless the automaton was built to interpret them.

## Treasure and Harvest


| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| servo node | 1 | Director-set |
| memory plate | 1 | Director-set |
| conductive wire | 1 | Director-set |

Servo nodes, memory plates, conductive wire, command lenses, and intact housings are prime Tinkering and Enchanting components.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change formation size, command priority, and terrain. Each added body should expand tactical geometry rather than simply add attacks.

knowledge.procedure: Retain each dossier's knowledge skill alternatives and its three actual DC thresholds. A focused identification attempt uses one real Search/Research Action in combat with actual observable signs or examined remains, or one uninterrupted minute of ordinary examination outside combat. Use the real acquired skill and underlying ability, actual helpers and conditions; no stat-block or hidden roster is supplied merely by selecting a UI row. tactics.originalHowItFights: It opens with **Sentinel Halberd** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Pressure Wave** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. When **Containment Pulse** recharges, it delays only if it can catch a more important cluster or interrupt a decisive ritual. It uses every action to preserve formation and converts broken lines into immediate repositioning.
tactics.originalHowToDefeat:
**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing, force damage.
- Spread before **Containment Pulse** becomes available.
- Bring forced movement and terrain creation.

**Combat Priority**

Split the formation and destroy the coordinating body.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **forced movement that breaks formation**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when Containment Pulse catches three or more Expedition members. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.
tactics.originalHabitat:
Drone zones favor grids, choke points, rotating doors, magnetic floors, and lines that improve formation attacks. Their positions are part of the stat block.

Order-Drones are collective constructs designed to solve movement, trespass, and containment problems through formation. A “pair,” “tetrad,” or “quintet” is one tactical intelligence distributed across several bodies.

Correct credentials, maintenance codes, or a higher-priority emergency may redirect them. Emotional appeals do nothing unless the automaton was built to interpret them.
tactics.procedure: At each actual regular START choose from the creature's real perceptions, remembered observations and declared objective: an actual legal source-specific objective/counter first; otherwise the printed How It Fights opening attack, a ready announced area only if its visible recipients suit the objective, then a legal native sequence. A failed path or unavailable target does not grant hidden location knowledge or teleportation. A territorial withdrawal decision and an intelligent surrender/parley are choices, not conditions that remove a player's agency. To disengage under threat the creature must spend its own actual Withdraw/Disengage Action and actual movement, or bear ordinary opportunity-attack risk; no guaranteed escape or unearned pursuit distance. Exact route geometry, hazards, loads and chase transitions come from actual EX58 inputs. Adjacent enemies, line of sight and cover are recomputed before each real movement segment. Real retreat leaves actual cargo, mounts, downed bodies and witness histories where their sources place them; success awards no second kill, material bundle, generic XP or faction change. An encounter boundary does not reset resource/source receipts unless their actual rule says it does.

source.originalUtf8Text:
# Pact Devil (Black Court)

**Family:** Pact Court
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T1, Floors 1-10
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

This Black Court agent embodies secrecy and erased witness. Its apparent color is a jurisdictional mark, not decoration, and the seal it carries determines which promises, names, and boundaries it can turn into force.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Wax with no heat source; footprints stopping at written boundaries; gifts arranged in court colors; a witness unable to describe what was promised but certain that it was fair. Heat appears in sealed metal before open flame.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Religion** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 11 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 15 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 19 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 1-10  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Medium Fiend, Lawful Evil**  
**Challenge** 1/2 (100 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T1 · **Floors** 1-10
**Armor** 12 · **Hit Points** 31 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 16 (+3) |

**Resistances** fire, necrotic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** frightened  
**Tactical Vulnerability** invalidated oath or court seal  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Court Seal.** The devil gains advantage when attacking a creature marked by a promise, brand, or accepted gift.

### Actions

**Hellfire Claw.** *Attack:* +4 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d6+2 fire damage (average 6).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Hellfire Claw** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It repeatedly tests for careless speech and marks the first character who accepts a benefit or answers on behalf of another.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for fire damage.
- Appoint one speaker and forbid casual promises.

**Combat Priority**

Invalidate the court seal or brand before committing to damage.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **invalidated oath or court seal**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Court chambers use marked thresholds, braziers, oath circles, and audience galleries. Position often determines which creature is considered witness, petitioner, debtor, or trespasser.

The Pact Courts are fiendish legal cultures organized by the kind of obligation they weaponize. Their colors are not moral categories. They are schools of coercion, memory, appetite, secrecy, and authority.

Pact devils prefer enforceable victories. They may withdraw from a profitable fight to preserve precedent.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Religion · **Harvest DC:** 12 · **Base time:** 20 minutes  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Animated Core (Tier 1) | 1 | 47%, 10 gp base |

Court seals, branded hide, oath-iron, furnace ash, and infernal marrow are valuable. The mark of ownership must be removed before sale or crafting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change court, seal, offered benefit, and default consequence. Mixed-court groups are unstable and may turn on one another when jurisdiction overlaps.

# Pact Devil (Blue Court)

**Family:** Pact Court
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T2, Floors 11-20
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

This Blue Court agent embodies memory and deferred payment. Its apparent color is a jurisdictional mark, not decoration, and the seal it carries determines which promises, names, and boundaries it can turn into force.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Wax with no heat source; footprints stopping at written boundaries; gifts arranged in court colors; a witness unable to describe what was promised but certain that it was fair.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Religion** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 11-20  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Medium Fiend, Lawful Evil**  
**Challenge** 2 (450 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T2 · **Floors** 11-20
**Armor** 13 · **Hit Points** 68 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 16 (+3) |

**Resistances** fire, necrotic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** frightened  
**Tactical Vulnerability** invalidated oath or court seal  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**Court Seal.** The devil gains advantage when attacking a creature marked by a promise, brand, or accepted gift.

### Actions

**Abyssal Rend.** *Attack:* +5 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d10+2 necrotic damage (average 8).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Abyssal Rend** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It repeatedly tests for careless speech and marks the first character who accepts a benefit or answers on behalf of another.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for necrotic damage.
- Appoint one speaker and forbid casual promises.

**Combat Priority**

Invalidate the court seal or brand before committing to damage.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **invalidated oath or court seal**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Court chambers use marked thresholds, braziers, oath circles, and audience galleries. Position often determines which creature is considered witness, petitioner, debtor, or trespasser.

The Pact Courts are fiendish legal cultures organized by the kind of obligation they weaponize. Their colors are not moral categories. They are schools of coercion, memory, appetite, secrecy, and authority.

Pact devils prefer enforceable victories. They may withdraw from a profitable fight to preserve precedent.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Religion · **Harvest DC:** 12 · **Base time:** 30 minutes  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Beast Hide (Tier 1) | 1 | 54%, 12 gp base |
| Sharp Fang (Tier 2) | 2 | 45%, 24 gp base |

Court seals, branded hide, oath-iron, furnace ash, and infernal marrow are valuable. The mark of ownership must be removed before sale or crafting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change court, seal, offered benefit, and default consequence. Mixed-court groups are unstable and may turn on one another when jurisdiction overlaps.

# Pact Devil (Green Court)

**Family:** Pact Court
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

This Green Court agent embodies appetite, envy, and possession. Its apparent color is a jurisdictional mark, not decoration, and the seal it carries determines which promises, names, and boundaries it can turn into force.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Wax with no heat source; footprints stopping at written boundaries; gifts arranged in court colors; a witness unable to describe what was promised but certain that it was fair. Heat appears in sealed metal before open flame.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Religion** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 13 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 17 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 21 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Court agents sometimes demand the destruction of research rather than payment, suggesting that information itself can violate an older agreement. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Medium Fiend, Lawful Evil**  
**Challenge** 12 (8400 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 17 · **Hit Points** 404 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 17 (+3) | 15 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 18 (+4) |

**Resistances** fire, necrotic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** frightened  
**Tactical Vulnerability** invalidated oath or court seal  
**Save DC** 17  

### Traits

**Court Seal.** The devil gains advantage when attacking a creature marked by a promise, brand, or accepted gift.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Hellfire Claw.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d8+9 fire damage (average 22).

**Soul Burn.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d8+8 fire damage (average 22).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Hellfire Claw** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Soul Burn** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It repeatedly tests for careless speech and marks the first character who accepts a benefit or answers on behalf of another.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for fire damage.
- Appoint one speaker and forbid casual promises.

**Combat Priority**

Invalidate the court seal or brand before committing to damage.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **invalidated oath or court seal**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line; resources fall below half before the arena mechanic is solved. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Court chambers use marked thresholds, braziers, oath circles, and audience galleries. Position often determines which creature is considered witness, petitioner, debtor, or trespasser.

The Pact Courts are fiendish legal cultures organized by the kind of obligation they weaponize. Their colors are not moral categories. They are schools of coercion, memory, appetite, secrecy, and authority.

Pact devils prefer enforceable victories. They may withdraw from a profitable fight to preserve precedent.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Religion · **Harvest DC:** 16 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| oath-iron | 2 | Director-set |
| infernal marrow | 2 | Director-set |
| court seal | 2 | Director-set |

**Known recipe links:** Sovereign Graveburst Flask, Greater Grave Axe, Relic Grave Hammer, Exalted Infernal Marrow Soup.

Court seals, branded hide, oath-iron, furnace ash, and infernal marrow are valuable. The mark of ownership must be removed before sale or crafting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change court, seal, offered benefit, and default consequence. Mixed-court groups are unstable and may turn on one another when jurisdiction overlaps.

# Pact Devil (Red Court)

**Family:** Pact Court
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

This Red Court agent embodies violence, urgency, and blood price. Its apparent color is a jurisdictional mark, not decoration, and the seal it carries determines which promises, names, and boundaries it can turn into force.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Wax with no heat source; footprints stopping at written boundaries; gifts arranged in court colors; a witness unable to describe what was promised but certain that it was fair. Heat appears in sealed metal before open flame.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Religion** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 13 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 17 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 21 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Court agents sometimes demand the destruction of research rather than payment, suggesting that information itself can violate an older agreement. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Large Fiend, Lawful Evil**  
**Challenge** 9 (5000 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 16 · **Hit Points** 314 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 17 (+3) | 14 (+2) | 16 (+3) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 17 (+3) |

**Resistances** fire, necrotic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** frightened  
**Tactical Vulnerability** invalidated oath or court seal  
**Save DC** 15  

### Traits

**Court Seal.** The devil gains advantage when attacking a creature marked by a promise, brand, or accepted gift.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Infernal Strike.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+8 fire damage (average 19).

**Soul Burn.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+7 fire damage (average 18).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Infernal Strike** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Soul Burn** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It repeatedly tests for careless speech and marks the first character who accepts a benefit or answers on behalf of another.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for fire damage.
- Appoint one speaker and forbid casual promises.

**Combat Priority**

Invalidate the court seal or brand before committing to damage.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **invalidated oath or court seal**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Court chambers use marked thresholds, braziers, oath circles, and audience galleries. Position often determines which creature is considered witness, petitioner, debtor, or trespasser.

The Pact Courts are fiendish legal cultures organized by the kind of obligation they weaponize. Their colors are not moral categories. They are schools of coercion, memory, appetite, secrecy, and authority.

Pact devils prefer enforceable victories. They may withdraw from a profitable fight to preserve precedent.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Religion · **Harvest DC:** 15 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Radiant Feather (Tier 1) | 1 | 85%, 19 gp base |
| Blessed Essence (Tier 2) | 2 | 71%, 38 gp base |
| Holy Symbol (Tier 3) | 3 | 56%, 76 gp base |

Court seals, branded hide, oath-iron, furnace ash, and infernal marrow are valuable. The mark of ownership must be removed before sale or crafting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change court, seal, offered benefit, and default consequence. Mixed-court groups are unstable and may turn on one another when jurisdiction overlaps.

# Pact Devil (White Court)

**Family:** Pact Court
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Striker

## What It Is

This White Court agent embodies authority, purity, and exclusion. Its apparent color is a jurisdictional mark, not decoration, and the seal it carries determines which promises, names, and boundaries it can turn into force.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Wax with no heat source; footprints stopping at written boundaries; gifts arranged in court colors; a witness unable to describe what was promised but certain that it was fair. Heat appears in sealed metal before open flame.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Religion** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Court registries, infernal contracts, and licensed negotiator reports  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Court agents sometimes demand the destruction of research rather than payment, suggesting that information itself can violate an older agreement. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Medium Fiend, Lawful Evil**  
**Challenge** 7 (2900 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 246 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 16 (+3) |

**Resistances** fire, necrotic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** frightened  
**Tactical Vulnerability** invalidated oath or court seal  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**Court Seal.** The devil gains advantage when attacking a creature marked by a promise, brand, or accepted gift.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Hellfire Claw.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+8 fire damage (average 17).

**Soul Burn.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+7 fire damage (average 16).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Hellfire Claw** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Soul Burn** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It repeatedly tests for careless speech and marks the first character who accepts a benefit or answers on behalf of another.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for fire damage.
- Appoint one speaker and forbid casual promises.

**Combat Priority**

Invalidate the court seal or brand before committing to damage.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **invalidated oath or court seal**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Court chambers use marked thresholds, braziers, oath circles, and audience galleries. Position often determines which creature is considered witness, petitioner, debtor, or trespasser.

The Pact Courts are fiendish legal cultures organized by the kind of obligation they weaponize. Their colors are not moral categories. They are schools of coercion, memory, appetite, secrecy, and authority.

Pact devils prefer enforceable victories. They may withdraw from a profitable fight to preserve precedent.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Religion · **Harvest DC:** 14 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Strange Tentacle (Tier 1) | 1 | 77%, 17 gp base |
| Aberrant Ichor (Tier 2) | 2 | 64%, 34 gp base |
| Mind Crystal (Tier 3) | 3 | 51%, 68 gp base |

Court seals, branded hide, oath-iron, furnace ash, and infernal marrow are valuable. The mark of ownership must be removed before sale or crafting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change court, seal, offered benefit, and default consequence. Mixed-court groups are unstable and may turn on one another when jurisdiction overlaps.

**Dungeon range:** T2, Floors 11-20
**Primary source:** Apothecaries’ Collegium, marsh wardens, and sanctioned harvest crews
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Skirmisher or social adversary

## What It Is

Poison-Skin is part of Bloomdeep’s economy of rot, medicine, hunger, and propagation. Its body and lair exchange material constantly, so killing the visible creature does not always end the encounter.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Bubbles moving against the current; mushrooms opening toward wounded creatures; bones polished clean without tooth marks; bright amphibian prints ending beneath stagnant water.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **History or Insight** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Apothecaries’ Collegium, marsh wardens, and sanctioned harvest crews  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 11-20  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Medium Humanoid, Neutral**  
**Challenge** 3 (700 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T2 · **Floors** 11-20
**Armor** 14 · **Hit Points** 88 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 12 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 11 (+0) |

**Resistances** None  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** airflow control and source-node destruction  
**Save DC** 11  

### Traits

**Living Substrate.** It can use roots, spores, corpses, or standing water in its lair as the origin point of one action.

### Actions

**Heavy Blow.** *Attack:* +5 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d6+2 bludgeoning damage (average 9).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Heavy Blow** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It turns corpses, spilled reagents, open wounds, and standing water into additional pressure.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning damage.
- Seal skin and breathing; separate fire from concentrated spores.

**Combat Priority**

Remove brood pools, root nodes, corpses, or chemical trails that sustain the creature.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **airflow control and source-node destruction**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Marsh lairs use water depth, root tunnels, spore pockets, floating ground, and corrosive pools. Fire solves some problems but can turn enclosed spores into explosions.

Bloomdeep turns hunger, rot, medicine, and reproduction into the same ecological process. Its creatures are dangerous because every wound, corpse, and abandoned ration can become part of the next encounter.

Sporefolk and Poison-Skins can negotiate. Grazers and crawlers are driven by chemical cues; changing scent may redirect them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Medicine · **Harvest DC:** 11 · **Base time:** 1 hour  
**Restriction:** Routine harvesting is culturally prohibited or legally restricted; samples require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play.

Venom, spores, glands, slime, hide, root fiber, and digestive acid are useful but spoil quickly and require separated containers.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change substrate, spore, toxin, or brood source. A clean battlefield makes these creatures weaker; an abandoned battlefield makes them stronger.

# Season-Bound Autumn

**Family:** Season-Bound
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Agricultural wardens, druidic calendars, and weather station logs
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Controller

## What It Is

The Autumn expression embodies ripeness, debt, and decay. It is drawn to places where the natural cycle has been accelerated, delayed, commercialized, or magically denied.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Plants acting one season ahead; insects emerging at the wrong temperature; frost preserving fresh blood; fruit ripening only when watched. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Nature or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |

| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Agricultural wardens, druidic calendars, and weather station logs  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

A few manifestations repeat seasons that never occurred in the surrounding region, including harvests of plants no scholar can identify. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Medium Fey, Neutral Good**  
**Challenge** 5 (1800 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 95 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 16 (+3) |

**Resistances** None  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** destruction of the seasonal anchor  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Seasonal Anchor.** While its anchor remains intact and inside the encounter area, it regenerates hit points equal to its tier at the start of its turn.

### Actions

**Glamour Cut.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+4 psychic damage (average 13).

**Mislead Strike.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+3 psychic damage (average 12).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Glamour Cut** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Mislead Strike** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It cycles terrain toward its season and avoids neutral ground.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic damage.
- Identify the seasonal anchor before damaging the body.

**Combat Priority**

Move the fight to a neutral boundary and break the seasonal anchor.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **destruction of the seasonal anchor**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

A Season-Bound site contains overlapping climates and zones of accelerated growth, heat, decay, or preservation. Crossing the wrong boundary can empower the creature.

Season-Bound are fey embodiments of transition rather than weather alone. Each appears when a place is forced to change too quickly or prevented from changing at all.

They can be reasoned with through cycles, exchanges, and timely sacrifice. Demanding permanence is offensive to most of them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Nature · **Harvest DC:** 11 · **Base time:** 30 minutes  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| sparkling petal | 1 | 68%, 15 gp base |
| glimmering leaf | 2 | 56%, 30 gp base |
| spirit blossom | 3 | 45%, 60 gp base |

**Known recipe links:** Minor Stormward Draught, Minor Stormward Draught — Sparkling Petal, Minor Storm Pie, Refined Storm Roast.

Pollen, sap, preserved petals, weathered bark, frost glands, and seasonal essence are valuable across Alchemy, Cooking, Herbalism, and Enchanting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the seasonal anchor and environmental boundary. Opposed seasons can appear together when a site is violently transitioning.

# Season-Bound Spring

**Family:** Season-Bound
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Agricultural wardens, druidic calendars, and weather station logs
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Striker

## What It Is

The Spring expression embodies growth that will not stop. It is drawn to places where the natural cycle has been accelerated, delayed, commercialized, or magically denied.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Plants acting one season ahead; insects emerging at the wrong temperature; frost preserving fresh blood; fruit ripening only when watched. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Nature or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Agricultural wardens, druidic calendars, and weather station logs  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

A few manifestations repeat seasons that never occurred in the surrounding region, including harvests of plants no scholar can identify. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Huge Fey, Neutral Evil**  
**Challenge** 6 (2300 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 224 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 21 (+5) | 12 (+1) | 15 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 16 (+3) |

**Resistances** None  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** destruction of the seasonal anchor  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Seasonal Anchor.** While its anchor remains intact and inside the encounter area, it regenerates hit points equal to its tier at the start of its turn.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Glamour Cut.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+6 psychic damage (average 15).

**Mislead Strike.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+5 psychic damage (average 14).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Glamour Cut** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Mislead Strike** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It cycles terrain toward its season and avoids neutral ground.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic damage.
- Identify the seasonal anchor before damaging the body.

**Combat Priority**

Move the fight to a neutral boundary and break the seasonal anchor.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **destruction of the seasonal anchor**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

A Season-Bound site contains overlapping climates and zones of accelerated growth, heat, decay, or preservation. Crossing the wrong boundary can empower the creature.

Season-Bound are fey embodiments of transition rather than weather alone. Each appears when a place is forced to change too quickly or prevented from changing at all.

They can be reasoned with through cycles, exchanges, and timely sacrifice. Demanding permanence is offensive to most of them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Nature · **Harvest DC:** 12 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Fey Dust (Tier 1) | 1 | 72%, 16 gp base |
| Enchanted Leaf (Tier 2) | 2 | 60%, 32 gp base |
| Magical Pollen (Tier 3) | 3 | 48%, 64 gp base |

Pollen, sap, preserved petals, weathered bark, frost glands, and seasonal essence are valuable across Alchemy, Cooking, Herbalism, and Enchanting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the seasonal anchor and environmental boundary. Opposed seasons can appear together when a site is violently transitioning.
