# Season-Bound Summer

**Family:** Season-Bound
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Agricultural wardens, druidic calendars, and weather station logs
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

The Summer expression embodies heat, abundance, and exhaustion. It is drawn to places where the natural cycle has been accelerated, delayed, commercialized, or magically denied.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Plants acting one season ahead; insects emerging at the wrong temperature; frost preserving fresh blood; fruit ripening only when watched. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Nature or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 13 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 17 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 21 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Agricultural wardens, druidic calendars, and weather station logs  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

A few manifestations repeat seasons that never occurred in the surrounding region, including harvests of plants no scholar can identify. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Huge Fey, True Neutral**  
**Challenge** 11 (7200 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 17 · **Hit Points** 374 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 21 (+5) | 13 (+1) | 16 (+3) | 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 17 (+3) |

**Resistances** None  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** destruction of the seasonal anchor  
**Save DC** 16  

### Traits

**Seasonal Anchor.** While its anchor remains intact and inside the encounter area, it regenerates hit points equal to its tier at the start of its turn.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Fey Whisper.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+9 psychic damage (average 20).

**Mislead Strike.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+8 psychic damage (average 19).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Fey Whisper** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Mislead Strike** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It cycles terrain toward its season and avoids neutral ground.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic damage.
- Identify the seasonal anchor before damaging the body.

**Combat Priority**

Move the fight to a neutral boundary and break the seasonal anchor.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **destruction of the seasonal anchor**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

A Season-Bound site contains overlapping climates and zones of accelerated growth, heat, decay, or preservation. Crossing the wrong boundary can empower the creature.

Season-Bound are fey embodiments of transition rather than weather alone. Each appears when a place is forced to change too quickly or prevented from changing at all.

They can be reasoned with through cycles, exchanges, and timely sacrifice. Demanding permanence is offensive to most of them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Nature · **Harvest DC:** 13 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| seasonal essence | 2 | Director-set |
| enchanted leaf | 2 | Director-set |
| magical pollen | 2 | Director-set |

Pollen, sap, preserved petals, weathered bark, frost glands, and seasonal essence are valuable across Alchemy, Cooking, Herbalism, and Enchanting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the seasonal anchor and environmental boundary. Opposed seasons can appear together when a site is violently transitioning.

- Identify the seasonal anchor before damaging the body.

**Combat Priority**

Move the fight to a neutral boundary and break the seasonal anchor.

The defining weakness is **destruction of the seasonal anchor**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

# Season-Bound Winter

**Family:** Season-Bound
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T2, Floors 11-20
**Primary source:** Agricultural wardens, druidic calendars, and weather station logs
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

The Winter expression embodies preservation, silence, and scarcity. It is drawn to places where the natural cycle has been accelerated, delayed, commercialized, or magically denied.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Plants acting one season ahead; insects emerging at the wrong temperature; frost preserving fresh blood; fruit ripening only when watched. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Nature or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Agricultural wardens, druidic calendars, and weather station logs  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 11-20  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Small Fey, Unaligned**  
**Challenge** 2 (450 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T2 · **Floors** 11-20
**Armor** 13 · **Hit Points** 68 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 9 (-1) | 16 (+3) | 13 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 16 (+3) |

**Resistances** None  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** destruction of the seasonal anchor  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**Seasonal Anchor.** While its anchor remains intact and inside the encounter area, it regenerates hit points equal to its tier at the start of its turn.

### Actions

**Fey Whisper.** *Attack:* +5 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d10+2 psychic damage (average 8).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Fey Whisper** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It cycles terrain toward its season and avoids neutral ground.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic damage.
- Identify the seasonal anchor before damaging the body.

**Combat Priority**

Move the fight to a neutral boundary and break the seasonal anchor.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **destruction of the seasonal anchor**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

A Season-Bound site contains overlapping climates and zones of accelerated growth, heat, decay, or preservation. Crossing the wrong boundary can empower the creature.

Season-Bound are fey embodiments of transition rather than weather alone. Each appears when a place is forced to change too quickly or prevented from changing at all.

They can be reasoned with through cycles, exchanges, and timely sacrifice. Demanding permanence is offensive to most of them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Nature · **Harvest DC:** 10 · **Base time:** 20 minutes  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Beast Hide (Tier 1) | 1 | 54%, 12 gp base |
| Sharp Fang (Tier 2) | 2 | 45%, 24 gp base |

Pollen, sap, preserved petals, weathered bark, frost glands, and seasonal essence are valuable across Alchemy, Cooking, Herbalism, and Enchanting.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the seasonal anchor and environmental boundary. Opposed seasons can appear together when a site is violently transitioning.

original.sourceText: While its anchor remains intact and inside the encounter area, it regenerates hit points equal to its tier at the start of its turn.

configuration.actualTierRequirement: Actual encounter floor T-tier, recorded before play; not CR, character level, damage rank, material tier or always the lowest listed tier. The example tier is a synthetic fixture value within the native source range.

traits.procedure: NEW SA02. Assign one real primary seasonal anchor, its current encounter area and actual floor T-tier. At each actual regular START while the creature is alive above0, that actual anchor is intact and inside the area, regain tier normal HP up to actual effective maximum under the real applicable healing prohibitions. Multiple anchors or duplicated callbacks do not multiply that one START event. An extra turn gives no new regular START recovery. A source that prevents HP gain still prevents it; no credit is banked. Real damage to or removal of the anchor stops future eligible gains without undoing past healing. Do not resurrect a dead/zero body, remove Wounds, change seasons globally or grant vulnerability to the opposite season.

A focused identification attempt uses one real Search/Research Action in combat with actual observable signs or examined remains, or one uninterrupted minute of ordinary examination outside combat. tactics.originalHowItFights: It opens with **Fey Whisper** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It cycles terrain toward its season and avoids neutral ground.
tactics.originalHowToDefeat:
**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic damage.
- Identify the seasonal anchor before damaging the body.

**Combat Priority**

Move the fight to a neutral boundary and break the seasonal anchor.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **destruction of the seasonal anchor**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.
tactics.originalHabitat:
A Season-Bound site contains overlapping climates and zones of accelerated growth, heat, decay, or preservation. Crossing the wrong boundary can empower the creature.

Season-Bound are fey embodiments of transition rather than weather alone. Each appears when a place is forced to change too quickly or prevented from changing at all.

They can be reasoned with through cycles, exchanges, and timely sacrifice. Demanding permanence is offensive to most of them.
tactics.procedure: At each actual regular START choose from the creature's real perceptions, remembered observations and declared objective: an actual legal source-specific objective/counter first; otherwise the printed How It Fights opening attack, a ready announced area only if its visible recipients suit the objective, then a legal native sequence. A failed path or unavailable target does not grant hidden location knowledge or teleportation. A territorial withdrawal decision and an intelligent surrender/parley are choices, not conditions that remove a player's agency. To disengage under threat the creature must spend its own actual Withdraw/Disengage Action and actual movement, or bear ordinary opportunity-attack risk; no guaranteed escape or unearned pursuit distance. Exact route geometry, hazards, loads and chase transitions come from actual EX58 inputs. Adjacent enemies, line of sight and cover are recomputed before each real movement segment. Real retreat leaves actual cargo, mounts, downed bodies and witness histories where their sources place them; success awards no second kill, material bundle, generic XP or faction change. An encounter boundary does not reset resource/source receipts unless their actual rule says it does.
tactics.arenaNarrativeBoundary: Gate test victory, alleged origins, memories and route rewards remain source narrative, not automatic hidden mechanics. An unprinted Seal Pulse is not a second new damage action; the printed recharge supplies the operational burst until separately authored evidence says otherwise.

phaseAndMovement.timeline: Cases supply numbered-round/turn identities as encounter fixtures; no global seconds-to-round mapping is adopted.
phaseAndMovement.terrainAndStances: Actual Dash/Withdraw/Guard/Brace/Ready/Hide/Search/Help and movement budgets use their accepted Core/Combat action procedures. Narrative Season-Bound Winter counterplay grants no free off-turn movement.
phaseAndMovement.gateAndArena: An actual arena/anchor is a scene input with real location and state. Missing scene content prevents that particular scene-dependent predicate, not the native damage attacks.
phaseAndMovement.formationMembership: Printed named units are single actors with explicit member IDs. Other nearby constructs are not joined or cloned by name; Sentinel networks require actual separate bodies.
phaseAndMovement.resetBoundary: No reset on body-fragment selection, mode transition, duplicate event, save/load or alternate route. Real source-ending/reset events retain their exact authority.

# Serpent-Blood Broodguard

**Family:** Deep Folk
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T2, Floors 11-20
**Primary source:** Haven treaty archives, captured correspondence, and parley reports
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Skirmisher or social adversary

## What It Is

Serpent-Blood Broodguard is an intelligent floor-dweller with territorial, religious, or political motives. Directors should establish what it protects before combat, because defeating it may create a worse enemy or close a valuable route.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Masonry repaired from the inside; water channels marked with votive cuts; discarded fungi sorted by toxicity; warning bolts deliberately embedded at eye level.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **History or Insight** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Haven treaty archives, captured correspondence, and parley reports  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 11-20  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Medium Humanoid, Lawful Evil**  
**Challenge** 1/4 (50 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T2 · **Floors** 11-20
**Armor** 12 · **Hit Points** 18 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 11 (+0) |

**Resistances** None  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** None identified  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**Prepared Ground.** It gains advantage on the first attack or check made from a fortified position in its lair.

### Actions

**Barbed Lash.** *Attack:* +3 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d6 slashing damage (average 4).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Barbed Lash** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses prepared cover and retreats behind the next defensive layer when the first is lost.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing damage.
- Map doors, bridges, and firing lanes before parley fails.

**Combat Priority**

Deny prepared terrain and command figures; accept surrender when the objective is secured.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **None identified**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Defended holds use layered doors, murder shafts, water traps, narrow bridges, and negotiated kill zones. Religious sites add chanting pools, toxin vents, and captive witnesses.

The deep folk are not one faction. They are cultures forced into the same trade roads, flooded caverns, and defensive wars. Their encounters should begin with motive before initiative.

Deep folk respond to ownership, passage rights, debts, clan names, and proof of common enemies.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Nature · **Harvest DC:** 10 · **Base time:** 10 minutes  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Magical Seed (Tier 1) | 1 | 46%, 10 gp base |

Humanoid harvesting is restricted. Salvage weapons, armor, mounts’ shed chitin, venom, ritual reagents, and legally claimed battlefield equipment instead.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change faction, passage rights, fortifications, and surrender terms. Intelligent foes should not be reskinned as mindless monsters.

# Spawn of the Worm Spiral

**Family:** Spiral
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T4, Floors 21-40
**Primary source:** Restricted research copies held by the Haven colleges
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

Spawn of the Worm Spiral is a product or cultivator of Spiral instability. Its anatomy should not be read as a stable species description; parts may change function when the breach, room geometry, or observer changes.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Repeated angles that do not close; echoes arriving before the sound; footprints on ceilings without disturbed dust; crystal growth turning toward empty air; headaches synchronized among several people.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Restricted research copies held by the Haven colleges  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-40

### Unsettling Evidence

The creature’s body repeats structures found in unrelated ruins. No accepted theory explains why different expeditions reproduce the same diagram without sharing notes. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

## Stat Block

**Large Aberration, Chaotic Neutral**  
**Challenge** 6 (2300 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T4 · **Floors** 21-40
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 168 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 17 (+3) | 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) |

**Resistances** psychic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** charmed  
**Tactical Vulnerability** stabilized geometry and vibration damping  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Unstable Geometry.** The first time each round a creature repeats the same movement path or action sequence, the monster gains a defensive reaction.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 2 attacks using the actions below.

**Heavy Blow.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+5 bludgeoning damage (average 14).

**Off-hand Strike.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+4 piercing damage (average 13).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Heavy Blow** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Off-hand Strike** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It changes angle, route, or target whenever the Expedition repeats a successful pattern.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning, piercing damage.
- Mark routes with physical cord and damp vibration.

**Combat Priority**

Stabilize or destroy the breach anchor before the room rewrites the fight.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **stabilized geometry and vibration damping**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Breach lairs are shaped by impossible shortcuts, thin walls, sudden gravity changes, and resonant surfaces. A straight retreat may return the party to the fight.

Spiral creatures arise where geometry, memory, and matter cease agreeing. Some are born animals altered by repeated exposure; others are organized broods that cultivate breaches and use them as roads, nurseries, or weapons.

Most breach fauna cannot bargain. Brood-Sages and certain Fracture-Kin can exchange information, but their concept of identity may not match the speaker’s.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Medicine · **Harvest DC:** 12 · **Base time:** 1 hour  
**Restriction:** Routine harvesting is culturally prohibited or legally restricted; samples require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play.  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Tribal Fetish (Tier 1) | 1 | 72%, 16 gp base |
| Crafted Item (Tier 2) | 2 | 60%, 32 gp base |
| Cultural Artifact (Tier 3) | 3 | 48%, 64 gp base |

Ichor, chitin, eyes, memory crystals, and breach residue are valuable but unstable. Preserve them in separated containers; two incompatible samples can begin reacting during transport.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the breach anchor and the rule it violates. Variants should alter routes, perception, or action repetition rather than only damage type.

# Spiral Breach Brood-Sage

**Family:** Spiral
**Knowledge status:** Restricted Deep Record
**Publication classification:** Deep-license reference
**Dungeon range:** T4-T5, Floors 31-50
**Primary source:** Restricted research copies held by the Haven colleges
**Reliability:** Moderate to high
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

Spiral Breach Brood-Sage is a product or cultivator of Spiral instability. Its anatomy should not be read as a stable species description; parts may change function when the breach, room geometry, or observer changes.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Repeated angles that do not close; echoes arriving before the sound; footprints on ceilings without disturbed dust; crystal growth turning toward empty air; headaches synchronized among several people. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 14 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 18 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 22 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Restricted Deep Record  
**Primary source:** Restricted research copies held by the Haven colleges  
**Reliability:** Moderate to high  
**Last confirmed:** Confirmed within the last two Openings  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 31-40  
**Rumored range:** Floors 41-50

### Unsettling Evidence

The creature’s body repeats structures found in unrelated ruins. No accepted theory explains why different expeditions reproduce the same diagram without sharing notes. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Huge Aberration, True Neutral**  
**Challenge** 13 (10000 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T4-T5 · **Floors** 31-50
**Armor** 18 · **Hit Points** 434 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 22 (+6) | 13 (+1) | 17 (+3) | 16 (+3) | 14 (+2) | 14 (+2) |

**Resistances** psychic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** charmed  
**Tactical Vulnerability** stabilized geometry and vibration damping  
**Save DC** 17  

### Traits

**Unstable Geometry.** The first time each round a creature repeats the same movement path or action sequence, the monster gains a defensive reaction.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Warped Tentacle.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d8+9 bludgeoning damage (average 22).

**Psychic Pulse.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d8+8 psychic damage (average 22).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Warped Tentacle** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Psychic Pulse** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It changes angle, route, or target whenever the Expedition repeats a successful pattern.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning, psychic damage.
- Mark routes with physical cord and damp vibration.

**Combat Priority**

Stabilize or destroy the breach anchor before the room rewrites the fight.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **stabilized geometry and vibration damping**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line; resources fall below half before the arena mechanic is solved. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Breach lairs are shaped by impossible shortcuts, thin walls, sudden gravity changes, and resonant surfaces. A straight retreat may return the party to the fight.

Spiral creatures arise where geometry, memory, and matter cease agreeing. Some are born animals altered by repeated exposure; others are organized broods that cultivate breaches and use them as roads, nurseries, or weapons.

Most breach fauna cannot bargain. Brood-Sages and certain Fracture-Kin can exchange information, but their concept of identity may not match the speaker’s.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Arcana · **Harvest DC:** 16 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Elemental Core (Tier 1) | 1 | 100%, 23 gp base |
| Pure Element (Tier 2) | 2 | 86%, 46 gp base |
| Primal Essence (Tier 3) | 3 | 69%, 92 gp base |
| Elemental Shard (Tier 4) | 4 | 52%, 184 gp base |

Ichor, chitin, eyes, memory crystals, and breach residue are valuable but unstable. Preserve them in separated containers; two incompatible samples can begin reacting during transport.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the breach anchor and the rule it violates. Variants should alter routes, perception, or action repetition rather than only damage type.

# Spiral Breach Ripper

**Family:** Spiral
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Restricted research copies held by the Haven colleges
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Striker

## What It Is

Spiral Breach Ripper is a product or cultivator of Spiral instability. Its anatomy should not be read as a stable species description; parts may change function when the breach, room geometry, or observer changes.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Repeated angles that do not close; echoes arriving before the sound; footprints on ceilings without disturbed dust; crystal growth turning toward empty air; headaches synchronized among several people. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Restricted research copies held by the Haven colleges  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

The creature’s body repeats structures found in unrelated ruins. No accepted theory explains why different expeditions reproduce the same diagram without sharing notes. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Huge Aberration, True Neutral**  
**Challenge** 6 (2300 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 224 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 21 (+5) | 12 (+1) | 15 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) |

**Resistances** psychic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** charmed  
**Tactical Vulnerability** stabilized geometry and vibration damping  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Unstable Geometry.** The first time each round a creature repeats the same movement path or action sequence, the monster gains a defensive reaction.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Warped Tentacle.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+6 bludgeoning damage (average 15).

**Psychic Pulse.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+5 psychic damage (average 14).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Warped Tentacle** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Psychic Pulse** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It changes angle, route, or target whenever the Expedition repeats a successful pattern.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning, psychic damage.
- Mark routes with physical cord and damp vibration.

**Combat Priority**

Stabilize or destroy the breach anchor before the room rewrites the fight.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **stabilized geometry and vibration damping**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Breach lairs are shaped by impossible shortcuts, thin walls, sudden gravity changes, and resonant surfaces. A straight retreat may return the party to the fight.

Spiral creatures arise where geometry, memory, and matter cease agreeing. Some are born animals altered by repeated exposure; others are organized broods that cultivate breaches and use them as roads, nurseries, or weapons.

Most breach fauna cannot bargain. Brood-Sages and certain Fracture-Kin can exchange information, but their concept of identity may not match the speaker’s.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Arcana · **Harvest DC:** 14 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Monstrous Claw (Tier 1) | 1 | 72%, 16 gp base |
| Exotic Hide (Tier 2) | 2 | 60%, 32 gp base |
| Venomous Gland (Tier 3) | 3 | 48%, 64 gp base |

Ichor, chitin, eyes, memory crystals, and breach residue are valuable but unstable. Preserve them in separated containers; two incompatible samples can begin reacting during transport.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the breach anchor and the rule it violates. Variants should alter routes, perception, or action repetition rather than only damage type.

# Spiral Worm

**Family:** Spiral
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T1, Floor 1
**Primary source:** Restricted research copies held by the Haven colleges
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

Spiral Worm is a product or cultivator of Spiral instability. Its anatomy should not be read as a stable species description; parts may change function when the breach, room geometry, or observer changes.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Repeated angles that do not close; echoes arriving before the sound; footprints on ceilings without disturbed dust; crystal growth turning toward empty air; headaches synchronized among several people. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 11 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 15 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 19 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Restricted research copies held by the Haven colleges  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 1-1  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Large Aberration, Chaotic Neutral**  
**Challenge** 2 (450 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T1 · **Floors** Floor 1
**Armor** 13 · **Hit Points** 68 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 (+3) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 15 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) |

**Resistances** psychic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** charmed  
**Tactical Vulnerability** stabilized geometry and vibration damping  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Unstable Geometry.** The first time each round a creature repeats the same movement path or action sequence, the monster gains a defensive reaction.

### Actions

**Void Rend.** *Attack:* +5 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d10+2 psychic damage (average 8).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Void Rend** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It changes angle, route, or target whenever the Expedition repeats a successful pattern.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic damage.
- Mark routes with physical cord and damp vibration.

**Combat Priority**

Stabilize or destroy the breach anchor before the room rewrites the fight.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **stabilized geometry and vibration damping**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Breach lairs are shaped by impossible shortcuts, thin walls, sudden gravity changes, and resonant surfaces. A straight retreat may return the party to the fight.

Spiral creatures arise where geometry, memory, and matter cease agreeing. Some are born animals altered by repeated exposure; others are organized broods that cultivate breaches and use them as roads, nurseries, or weapons.

Most breach fauna cannot bargain. Brood-Sages and certain Fracture-Kin can exchange information, but their concept of identity may not match the speaker’s.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Arcana · **Harvest DC:** 12 · **Base time:** 1 hour  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Elemental Core (Tier 1) | 1 | 54%, 12 gp base |
| Pure Element (Tier 2) | 2 | 45%, 24 gp base |

Ichor, chitin, eyes, memory crystals, and breach residue are valuable but unstable. Preserve them in separated containers; two incompatible samples can begin reacting during transport.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the breach anchor and the rule it violates. Variants should alter routes, perception, or action repetition rather than only damage type.

# Sporefolk Adult

**Family:** Bloomdeep
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T2, Floors 14-15
**Primary source:** Apothecaries’ Collegium, marsh wardens, and sanctioned harvest crews
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

Sporefolk Adult is part of Bloomdeep’s economy of rot, medicine, hunger, and propagation. Its body and lair exchange material constantly, so killing the visible creature does not always end the encounter.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Bubbles moving against the current; mushrooms opening toward wounded creatures; bones polished clean without tooth marks; bright amphibian prints ending beneath stagnant water.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Nature** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Apothecaries’ Collegium, marsh wardens, and sanctioned harvest crews  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 14-15  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Medium Plant, Neutral**  
**Challenge** 14 (11500 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T2 · **Floors** 14-15
**Armor** 18 · **Hit Points** 348 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 17 (+3) | 6 (-2) | 11 (+0) | 6 (-2) |

**Resistances** poison  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** airflow control and source-node destruction  
**Save DC** 18  

### Traits

**Living Substrate.** It can use roots, spores, corpses, or standing water in its lair as the origin point of one action.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 2 attacks using the actions below.

**Thorn Lash.** *Attack:* +9 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d8+9 piercing damage (average 22).

**Entangle.** *Attack:* +9 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 3d8+8 bludgeoning damage (average 22).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Thorn Lash** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Entangle** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It turns corpses, spilled reagents, open wounds, and standing water into additional pressure.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for piercing, bludgeoning damage.
- Seal skin and breathing; separate fire from concentrated spores.

**Combat Priority**

Remove brood pools, root nodes, corpses, or chemical trails that sustain the creature.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **airflow control and source-node destruction**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Marsh lairs use water depth, root tunnels, spore pockets, floating ground, and corrosive pools. Fire solves some problems but can turn enclosed spores into explosions.

Bloomdeep turns hunger, rot, medicine, and reproduction into the same ecological process. Its creatures are dangerous because every wound, corpse, and abandoned ration can become part of the next encounter.

Sporefolk and Poison-Skins can negotiate. Grazers and crawlers are driven by chemical cues; changing scent may redirect them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Nature · **Harvest DC:** 14 · **Base time:** 1 hour  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| living root | 1 | 100%, 24 gp base |
| animated vine | 2 | 90%, 48 gp base |
| toxic bud | 3 | 72%, 96 gp base |
| thistle heart | 4 | 54%, 192 gp base |

**Known recipe links:** Greater Living Root Cake, Minor Vital Soup, Minor Verdant Net, Refined Verdant Tackle.

Venom, spores, glands, slime, hide, root fiber, and digestive acid are useful but spoil quickly and require separated containers.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change substrate, spore, toxin, or brood source. A clean battlefield makes these creatures weaker; an abandoned battlefield makes them stronger.

# Sporefolk Sprout

**Family:** Bloomdeep
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T2, Floors 11-20
**Primary source:** Apothecaries’ Collegium, marsh wardens, and sanctioned harvest crews
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

Sporefolk Sprout is part of Bloomdeep’s economy of rot, medicine, hunger, and propagation. Its body and lair exchange material constantly, so killing the visible creature does not always end the encounter.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Bubbles moving against the current; mushrooms opening toward wounded creatures; bones polished clean without tooth marks; bright amphibian prints ending beneath stagnant water.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Nature** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Apothecaries’ Collegium, marsh wardens, and sanctioned harvest crews  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 11-20  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Small Plant, Neutral**  
**Challenge** 1/2 (100 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T2 · **Floors** 11-20
**Armor** 12 · **Hit Points** 31 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 9 (-1) | 16 (+3) | 13 (+1) | 5 (-3) | 10 (+0) | 5 (-3) |

**Resistances** poison  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** airflow control and source-node destruction  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**Living Substrate.** It can use roots, spores, corpses, or standing water in its lair as the origin point of one action.

### Actions

**Root Strike.** *Attack:* +4 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d6+2 bludgeoning damage (average 6).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Root Strike** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It turns corpses, spilled reagents, open wounds, and standing water into additional pressure.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning damage.
- Seal skin and breathing; separate fire from concentrated spores.

**Combat Priority**

Remove brood pools, root nodes, corpses, or chemical trails that sustain the creature.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **airflow control and source-node destruction**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Marsh lairs use water depth, root tunnels, spore pockets, floating ground, and corrosive pools. Fire solves some problems but can turn enclosed spores into explosions.

Bloomdeep turns hunger, rot, medicine, and reproduction into the same ecological process. Its creatures are dangerous because every wound, corpse, and abandoned ration can become part of the next encounter.

Sporefolk and Poison-Skins can negotiate. Grazers and crawlers are driven by chemical cues; changing scent may redirect them.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Nature · **Harvest DC:** 10 · **Base time:** 20 minutes  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| sticky sap | 1 | 47%, 10 gp base |

Venom, spores, glands, slime, hide, root fiber, and digestive acid are useful but spoil quickly and require separated containers.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change substrate, spore, toxin, or brood source. A clean battlefield makes these creatures weaker; an abandoned battlefield makes them stronger.

tactics.originalHowToDefeat:
**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for piercing, bludgeoning damage.
- Mark tremors and protect the rear line from resurfacing attacks.
- Spread before **Spore Burst** becomes available.

**Combat Priority**

Complete the arena objective while maintaining damage pressure.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **None identified**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when Spore Burst catches three or more Expedition members. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.
tactics.originalHabitat:
A Gate arena is part of the creature. Terrain, Seal Pulses, objectives, and failure conditions matter as much as hit points.

Gate Guardians are not random apex monsters. Each is a living examination tied to a Division of the dungeon, a Gate Seal, and a principle the Expedition must demonstrate under pressure.

Some Guardians speak, bargain, or test. None are safely reduced to ordinary patrons or quest-givers.

# Umbrin Arachnid

**Family:** Umbrin
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T1, Floors 1-10
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

Umbrin Arachnid is a bred hunting arachnid. Even when encountered alone, it is connected to a house objective, and surviving witnesses are likely to affect later negotiations.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Silk laid in deliberate geometric intervals; lamps hooded from the viewer rather than the corridor; cut gemstones left where a scout must choose whether to touch them; paired footprints that abruptly become one set.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Nature** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| DC 11 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 15 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 1-10  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Large Monstrosity, Unaligned**  
**Challenge** 1 (200 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T1 · **Floors** 1-10
**Armor** 13 · **Hit Points** 52 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 (+3) | 16 (+3) | 13 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 11 (+0) | 9 (-1) |

**Resistances** poison  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** bright-light disruption (tactical)  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**House-trained Darkvision.** Bright light disrupts its stealth routes, but ordinary darkness does not impair it.

### Actions

**Barbed Lash.** *Attack:* +4 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d8+2 slashing damage (average 6).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Barbed Lash** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It fights from darkness and vertical routes, spending lives only when a house objective justifies the cost.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing damage.
- Use broad illumination and cut silk routes.

**Combat Priority**

Remove the shadowblade or arachnomancer route network, then isolate command.

Umbrin sites emphasize verticality, narrow sight lines, web bridges, false balconies, and concealed side galleries. Their fighters know every line that can be crossed without entering bright light.

The Umbrin are a subterranean people whose houses treat darkness, silk, memory, and debt as instruments of government. Their patrols are not random dungeon encounters; each is an extension of a house policy, vendetta, or negotiation.

They respect accurate names, witnessed bargains, and demonstrated restraint. Threats against children, eggs, or house memory usually end negotiation immediately.

Umbrin Arachnomancer is a silk-mage and brood handler. Even when encountered alone, it is connected to a house objective, and surviving witnesses are likely to affect later negotiations.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Silk laid in deliberate geometric intervals; lamps hooded from the viewer rather than the corridor; cut gemstones left where a scout must choose whether to touch them; paired footprints that abruptly become one set.

Older house records describe sealed routes with no destination, maintained at great cost and never used for trade. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

**Off-hand Strike.** *Attack:* +6 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+5 piercing damage (average 14).

It opens with **Weapon Strike** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Off-hand Strike** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It fights from darkness and vertical routes, spending lives only when a house objective justifies the cost.

Umbrin sites emphasize verticality, narrow sight lines, web bridges, false balconies, and concealed side galleries. Their fighters know every line that can be crossed without entering bright light.

They respect accurate names, witnessed bargains, and demonstrated restraint. Threats against children, eggs, or house memory usually end negotiation immediately.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Medicine · **Harvest DC:** 12 · **Base time:** 2 hours  
**Restriction:** Routine harvesting is culturally prohibited or legally restricted; samples require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play.

Routine body harvesting is unlawful or culturally explosive. Equipment, venom, shed chitin, silk, and battlefield salvage are the safer sources of components.

Change house allegiance, objective, silk tools, and one role ability before changing hit points. An Umbrin encounter becomes memorable when the party can identify whose policy it represents.

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing, piercing damage.
- Use broad illumination and cut silk routes.

**Combat Priority**

Remove the shadowblade or arachnomancer route network, then isolate command.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **bright-light disruption (tactical)**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.
tactics.originalHabitat:
Umbrin sites emphasize verticality, narrow sight lines, web bridges, false balconies, and concealed side galleries. Their fighters know every line that can be crossed without entering bright light.

The Umbrin are a subterranean people whose houses treat darkness, silk, memory, and debt as instruments of government. Their patrols are not random dungeon encounters; each is an extension of a house policy, vendetta, or negotiation.

They respect accurate names, witnessed bargains, and demonstrated restraint. Threats against children, eggs, or house memory usually end negotiation immediately.

# Umbrin Favored Consort

**Family:** Umbrin
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T2, Floors 11-20
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Skirmisher or social adversary

## What It Is

Umbrin Favored Consort is a trusted witness and intermediary. Even when encountered alone, it is connected to a house objective, and surviving witnesses are likely to affect later negotiations.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Silk laid in deliberate geometric intervals; lamps hooded from the viewer rather than the corridor; cut gemstones left where a scout must choose whether to touch them; paired footprints that abruptly become one set.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **History or Insight** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 11-20  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Medium Humanoid, Neutral**  
**Challenge** 2 (450 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T2 · **Floors** 11-20
**Armor** 13 · **Hit Points** 68 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12 (+1) | 16 (+3) | 13 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 11 (+0) |

**Resistances** poison  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** bright-light disruption (tactical)  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**House-trained Darkvision.** Bright light disrupts its stealth routes, but ordinary darkness does not impair it.

### Actions

**Weapon Strike.** *Attack:* +5 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d10+2 slashing damage (average 8).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Weapon Strike** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It fights from darkness and vertical routes, spending lives only when a house objective justifies the cost.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing damage.
- Use broad illumination and cut silk routes.

**Combat Priority**

Remove the shadowblade or arachnomancer route network, then isolate command.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **bright-light disruption (tactical)**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Umbrin sites emphasize verticality, narrow sight lines, web bridges, false balconies, and concealed side galleries. Their fighters know every line that can be crossed without entering bright light.

The Umbrin are a subterranean people whose houses treat darkness, silk, memory, and debt as instruments of government. Their patrols are not random dungeon encounters; each is an extension of a house policy, vendetta, or negotiation.

They respect accurate names, witnessed bargains, and demonstrated restraint. Threats against children, eggs, or house memory usually end negotiation immediately.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Medicine · **Harvest DC:** 10 · **Base time:** 1 hour  
**Restriction:** Routine harvesting is culturally prohibited or legally restricted; samples require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play.  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Beast Hide (Tier 1) | 1 | 54%, 12 gp base |
| Sharp Fang (Tier 2) | 2 | 45%, 24 gp base |

Routine body harvesting is unlawful or culturally explosive. Equipment, venom, shed chitin, silk, and battlefield salvage are the safer sources of components.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change house allegiance, objective, silk tools, and one role ability before changing hit points. An Umbrin encounter becomes memorable when the party can identify whose policy it represents.

tactics.originalHowItFights: It opens with **Weapon Strike** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It fights from darkness and vertical routes, spending lives only when a house objective justifies the cost.
tactics.originalHowToDefeat:
**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing damage.
- Use broad illumination and cut silk routes.

**Combat Priority**

Remove the shadowblade or arachnomancer route network, then isolate command.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **bright-light disruption (tactical)**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.
tactics.originalHabitat:
Umbrin sites emphasize verticality, narrow sight lines, web bridges, false balconies, and concealed side galleries. Their fighters know every line that can be crossed without entering bright light.

The Umbrin are a subterranean people whose houses treat darkness, silk, memory, and debt as instruments of government. Their patrols are not random dungeon encounters; each is an extension of a house policy, vendetta, or negotiation.

They respect accurate names, witnessed bargains, and demonstrated restraint. Threats against children, eggs, or house memory usually end negotiation immediately.
tactics.procedure: At each actual regular START choose from the creature's real perceptions, remembered observations and declared objective: an actual legal source-specific objective/counter first; otherwise the printed How It Fights opening attack, a ready announced area only if its visible recipients suit the objective, then a legal native sequence. A failed path or unavailable target does not grant hidden location knowledge or teleportation. A territorial withdrawal decision and an intelligent surrender/parley are choices, not conditions that remove a player's agency. To disengage under threat the creature must spend its own actual Withdraw/Disengage Action and actual movement, or bear ordinary opportunity-attack risk; no guaranteed escape or unearned pursuit distance. Exact route geometry, hazards, loads and chase transitions come from actual EX58 inputs. Adjacent enemies, line of sight and cover are recomputed before each real movement segment. Real retreat leaves actual cargo, mounts, downed bodies and witness histories where their sources place them; success awards no second kill, material bundle, generic XP or faction change. An encounter boundary does not reset resource/source receipts unless their actual rule says it does.
tactics.arenaNarrativeBoundary: Gate test victory, alleged origins, memories and route rewards remain source narrative, not automatic hidden mechanics. source.originalUtf8Text:
# Umbrin Mage

**Family:** Umbrin
**Knowledge status:** Restricted Deep Record
**Publication classification:** Deep-license reference
**Dungeon range:** T4-T5, Floors 31-50
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records
**Reliability:** Moderate to high
**Encounter role:** Brute or anchor

## What It Is

Umbrin Mage is a battle scholar. Even when encountered alone, it is connected to a house objective, and surviving witnesses are likely to affect later negotiations.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Silk laid in deliberate geometric intervals; lamps hooded from the viewer rather than the corridor; cut gemstones left where a scout must choose whether to touch them; paired footprints that abruptly become one set. Different witnesses remember the same sound differently.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **History or Insight** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 13 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 17 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 21 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Restricted Deep Record  
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records  
**Reliability:** Moderate to high  
**Last confirmed:** Confirmed within the last two Openings  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 31-40  
**Rumored range:** Floors 41-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Older house records describe sealed routes with no destination, maintained at great cost and never used for trade. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Medium Humanoid, Lawful Neutral**  
**Challenge** 11 (7200 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T4-T5 · **Floors** 31-50
**Armor** 17 · **Hit Points** 374 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 (+1) | 16 (+3) | 16 (+3) | 12 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 12 (+1) |

**Resistances** poison  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** bright-light disruption (tactical)  
**Save DC** 16  

### Traits

**House-trained Darkvision.** Bright light disrupts its stealth routes, but ordinary darkness does not impair it.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Shadow Bolt.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+9 psychic damage (average 20).

**Off-hand Strike.** *Attack:* +8 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d10+8 piercing damage (average 19).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Shadow Bolt** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Off-hand Strike** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It fights from darkness and vertical routes, spending lives only when a house objective justifies the cost.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for psychic, piercing damage.
- Use broad illumination and cut silk routes.

**Combat Priority**

Remove the shadowblade or arachnomancer route network, then isolate command.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **bright-light disruption (tactical)**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Umbrin sites emphasize verticality, narrow sight lines, web bridges, false balconies, and concealed side galleries. Their fighters know every line that can be crossed without entering bright light.

The Umbrin are a subterranean people whose houses treat darkness, silk, memory, and debt as instruments of government. Their patrols are not random dungeon encounters; each is an extension of a house policy, vendetta, or negotiation.

They respect accurate names, witnessed bargains, and demonstrated restraint. Threats against children, eggs, or house memory usually end negotiation immediately.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Medicine · **Harvest DC:** 13 · **Base time:** 2 hours  
**Restriction:** Routine harvesting is culturally prohibited or legally restricted; samples require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play.  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Radiant Feather (Tier 1) | 1 | 95%, 21 gp base |
| Blessed Essence (Tier 2) | 2 | 79%, 42 gp base |
| Holy Symbol (Tier 3) | 3 | 63%, 84 gp base |
| Divine Light (Tier 4) | 4 | 47%, 168 gp base |

Routine body harvesting is unlawful or culturally explosive. Equipment, venom, shed chitin, silk, and battlefield salvage are the safer sources of components.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change house allegiance, objective, silk tools, and one role ability before changing hit points. An Umbrin encounter becomes memorable when the party can identify whose policy it represents.

# Umbrin Matron

**Family:** Umbrin
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Skirmisher or social adversary

## What It Is

Umbrin Matron is a political center of a house. Even when encountered alone, it is connected to a house objective, and surviving witnesses are likely to affect later negotiations.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Silk laid in deliberate geometric intervals; lamps hooded from the viewer rather than the corridor; cut gemstones left where a scout must choose whether to touch them; paired footprints that abruptly become one set.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **History or Insight** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Older house records describe sealed routes with no destination, maintained at great cost and never used for trade. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Medium Humanoid, Lawful Evil**  
**Challenge** 7 (2900 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 184 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 (+1) | 16 (+3) | 15 (+2) | 12 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 11 (+0) |

**Resistances** poison  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** bright-light disruption (tactical)  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**House-trained Darkvision.** Bright light disrupts its stealth routes, but ordinary darkness does not impair it.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 2 attacks using the actions below.

**Weapon Strike.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+6 slashing damage (average 15).

**Off-hand Strike.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+5 piercing damage (average 14).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Weapon Strike** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Off-hand Strike** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It fights from darkness and vertical routes, spending lives only when a house objective justifies the cost.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing, piercing damage.
- Use broad illumination and cut silk routes.

**Combat Priority**

Remove the shadowblade or arachnomancer route network, then isolate command.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **bright-light disruption (tactical)**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Umbrin sites emphasize verticality, narrow sight lines, web bridges, false balconies, and concealed side galleries. Their fighters know every line that can be crossed without entering bright light.

The Umbrin are a subterranean people whose houses treat darkness, silk, memory, and debt as instruments of government. Their patrols are not random dungeon encounters; each is an extension of a house policy, vendetta, or negotiation.

They respect accurate names, witnessed bargains, and demonstrated restraint. Threats against children, eggs, or house memory usually end negotiation immediately.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Medicine · **Harvest DC:** 12 · **Base time:** 1 hour  
**Restriction:** Routine harvesting is culturally prohibited or legally restricted; samples require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play.  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Strange Tentacle (Tier 1) | 1 | 77%, 17 gp base |
| Aberrant Ichor (Tier 2) | 2 | 64%, 34 gp base |
| Mind Crystal (Tier 3) | 3 | 51%, 68 gp base |

Routine body harvesting is unlawful or culturally explosive. Equipment, venom, shed chitin, silk, and battlefield salvage are the safer sources of components.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change house allegiance, objective, silk tools, and one role ability before changing hit points. An Umbrin encounter becomes memorable when the party can identify whose policy it represents.

# Umbrin Shadowblade

**Family:** Umbrin
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T1, Floors 1-10
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Skirmisher or social adversary

## What It Is

Umbrin Shadowblade is a infiltrator and executioner. Even when encountered alone, it is connected to a house objective, and surviving witnesses are likely to affect later negotiations.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Silk laid in deliberate geometric intervals; lamps hooded from the viewer rather than the corridor; cut gemstones left where a scout must choose whether to touch them; paired footprints that abruptly become one set.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **History or Insight** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 11 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 15 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 19 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Treaty delegations, undercity reports, and recovered house records  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 1-10  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Medium Humanoid, Neutral Evil**  
**Challenge** 7 (2900 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T1 · **Floors** 1-10
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 184 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 (+1) | 16 (+3) | 15 (+2) | 12 (+1) | 12 (+1) | 11 (+0) |

**Resistances** poison  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** None  
**Tactical Vulnerability** bright-light disruption (tactical)  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**House-trained Darkvision.** Bright light disrupts its stealth routes, but ordinary darkness does not impair it.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 2 attacks using the actions below.

**Precise Cut.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+6 slashing damage (average 15).

**Off-hand Strike.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+5 piercing damage (average 14).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Precise Cut** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Off-hand Strike** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It fights from darkness and vertical routes, spending lives only when a house objective justifies the cost.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for slashing, piercing damage.
- Use broad illumination and cut silk routes.

**Combat Priority**

Remove the shadowblade or arachnomancer route network, then isolate command.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **bright-light disruption (tactical)**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Umbrin sites emphasize verticality, narrow sight lines, web bridges, false balconies, and concealed side galleries. Their fighters know every line that can be crossed without entering bright light.

The Umbrin are a subterranean people whose houses treat darkness, silk, memory, and debt as instruments of government. Their patrols are not random dungeon encounters; each is an extension of a house policy, vendetta, or negotiation.

They respect accurate names, witnessed bargains, and demonstrated restraint. Threats against children, eggs, or house memory usually end negotiation immediately.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Medicine · **Harvest DC:** 12 · **Base time:** 1 hour  
**Restriction:** Routine harvesting is culturally prohibited or legally restricted; samples require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play.  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| Giant Bone (Tier 1) | 1 | 77%, 17 gp base |
| Massive Tooth (Tier 2) | 2 | 64%, 34 gp base |
| Thick Skin (Tier 3) | 3 | 51%, 68 gp base |

Routine body harvesting is unlawful or culturally explosive. Equipment, venom, shed chitin, silk, and battlefield salvage are the safer sources of components.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change house allegiance, objective, silk tools, and one role ability before changing hit points. An Umbrin encounter becomes memorable when the party can identify whose policy it represents.
